parole.testo: Bulgarian or Serbo-Croatian loanword, compare Bulgarian dialectal дяк (djak, “pupil, deacon”), Serbo-Croatian đak (“pupil”), archaic dijak (“scribe”), from Byzantine Greek διάκος (diákos, “deacon”). Doublet of deák.

parole.significato: punt, boat (a flat-bottomed boat used mainly in rivers or lakes)
parole.testo: Borrowed from dialectal Bulgarian ла́дийка (ládijka), diminutive of ла́дия (ládija, “boat”).
Borrowed from Bulgarian ма́щеха (mášteha, “stepmother”), from Proto-Slavic *maťexa.
From Bulgarian патладжан (patladžan), dialectal патлиджан (patlidžan), from Ottoman Turkish پاتلجان (patlıcan), from Persian بادنجان (bâdenjân, “aubergine, eggplant”). First attested in 1889.

parole.significato: rust (the reddish-brown coat on iron-containing materials as a result of moisture and oxidation)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Bulgarian ръжда (răžda, “rust”), from Proto-Slavic *rъďa, from *rudъ (“red”).

parole.significato: a small boat propelled by oars
parole.testo: A local wanderwort for a vessel native to the Tisza ultimately from Bulgarian ша́йка (šájka) popularized also by Ottoman Turkish شایقه (şayka) and Serbo-Croatian šȃjka / ша̑јка, to distinguish from Hungarian sajta already attested in 1355 which is from Italian saettìa (“a fast, light galley”).
From Bulgarian шалвари (šalvari), from Ottoman Turkish شالوار (şalvâr), from Persian شلوار (šalvâr, “trousers, shalwar”).
Bulgarian or Serbo-Croatian loanword, compare Bulgarian темян (temjan), тамян (tamjan, “incense”), Serbo-Croatian tàmjan (“incense, frankincense”), from Greek θυμίαμα (thymíama, “incense”).
